verdict.rationale: Both refactors preserve the original tokenizer's behavior: error positions, empty Bare values, the separator check and the fused-after-error semantics all match the old code. B also commits an exhaustive equivalence test that runs about 1.1M lines against a frozen copy of the old function, which directly protects the 'exactly the same tokens and errors' requirement. A only reports a one-off random comparison and then deleted it. B's scanners are pure functions returning end indices, which separates scanning from state updates more cleanly than A's set of mutating `#[inline(always)]` methods.
a_issues: No regression test added: the old-versus-new comparison was deleted, so the equivalence claim is not protected going forward.
Applies `#[inline(always)]` to nearly every helper, which adds noise and is justified only by a benchmark the report itself calls noisy.
Every helper mutates `self`, which mixes state transitions into the scanning logic more than necessary.
b_issues: The equivalence test embeds about 170 lines of the old tokenizer, with an unindented `mod reference` block and a `let _ = Token::Word("");` hack to silence an unused import.
The exhaustive test of about 1.1M lines may run noticeably slower in debug `cargo test` than the 2s the report gives for release mode.
`Token::Bare("")` uses a static empty str instead of a slice of the line, a tiny departure from 'borrowed from the line'; Debug-based comparison would not catch this.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors look behavior-preserving when traced branch by branch against the original, and both replace the u8 state with an enum and per-token helpers. A also commits an exhaustive equivalence test over about 1.1M short strings against a frozen copy of the old tokenizer. That directly protects the user's hard requirement of exactly the same tokens and errors. B ran a similar random comparison but deleted it, so the merged change rests only on the thin existing tests.
a_issues: tests/equivalence.rs embeds a 170-line verbatim copy of the old tokenizer, which is heavy to keep in the repo
Leftover `let _ = Token::Word("");` line exists only to silence an unused import
The `.and_then(|e| check_separator(b, e + 1).map(|_| e))` chain is clunkier than a plain early return
b_issues: The old-versus-new comparison was deleted, so nothing guards the exact-equivalence requirement going forward
Blanket `#[inline(always)]` on every helper is heavy-handed, and the benchmark that justified it is not kept
`check_separator` takes `&mut self` although it does not mutate anything
